title: Setup, Linux basics and Git
summary: First day: set up my Ubuntu server, hit three different SSH errors and fixed them, learned how Linux groups really work, and resolved my first Git merge conflict.

title: JavaScript core, Node.js and a password generator
summary: Learned the JavaScript basics properly, set up Node.js, and built a secure password generator with tests that I saw both pass and fail. This one took me two days.

title: Async JavaScript and debugging
summary: Learned how the event loop decides the order of code, why Promise.all is faster, how to read a stack trace, and how to pause a program with breakpoints in VS Code and Chrome DevTools.

title: Ports, TCP and sockets
summary: Built a TCP echo server on my Ubuntu machine, watched the three-way handshake with tcpdump, scanned ports with nmap, and learned why 'connection refused' and 'timed out' point to different problems.

title: DNS and HTTP from first principles
summary: Traced my own domain from the root servers, built an HTTP server with no framework on my Ubuntu machine, typed HTTP requests by hand, and broke every step of loading a page to learn which error message belongs to which step.

title: Debugging from the browser with DevTools
summary: Built a page with bugs on purpose and found each one from Chrome DevTools: uncaught errors in the Console, failed requests in the Network tab, a CORS block, a crashed server, and why 'Failed to fetch' alone tells you nothing.

title: React fundamentals, VaultLab's first front end
summary: Started VaultLab's real front end with React and Vite: components, props, state and loading data through a proxy. Then broke it in eight ways, including a white screen and a key bug that revealed the wrong password.

title: Express.js, VaultLab's real API
summary: Built VaultLab's real API with Express: REST routes with validation, a request logger, one error handler and a JSON 404, and connected the React app so items survive a reload. Then broke it in eight ways, and found out my firewall had been off the whole time.

title: Databases, VaultLab's items in MariaDB
summary: Moved VaultLab's items into MariaDB with a least-privilege user, wrote SQL by hand and rolled back an UPDATE without WHERE, then ran an SQL injection against my own search and fixed it with parameterized queries.

title: Authentication, hashing and sessions
summary: Gave VaultLab user accounts: login passwords hashed with scrypt, sessions in HttpOnly cookies stored only as hashes, and a protected items API. Then attacked my own login to see why each protection exists, from timing leaks to a logout that didn't log out.

title: Authorization, every user sees only their own vault
summary: Gave every vault item an owner, limited every query to the logged-in user, and added roles with an admin-only route. Then attacked my own API as a second user to see four classic authorization bugs: IDOR, 403 leaks, mass assignment and front-end-only checks.

title: Encryption, vault passwords you can read back but nobody else can
summary: Encrypted every vault password with AES-256-GCM, migrated the real data in three steps, and made the server refuse to start with a key that doesn't open the vault. Then broke my own encryption five ways: wrong key, a skipped check, a changed value, a copied value and a reused IV.

title: HTTPS and TLS, with nginx and my own CA
summary: Watched my own login cross the network in plain text, then put nginx in front with HTTPS, a certificate from my own small CA with a name constraint, HSTS and the API on loopback. Then broke it seven ways, from an untrusted CA and an expired certificate to a 502 and a trust proxy setting that lets attackers forge their address.

title: VaultLab as a systemd service
summary: Turned the API from a terminal tab into a hardened systemd service with its own user and a root-only secrets file, then broke it eight ways and learned to read crashes, crash loops and start failures from systemctl and journalctl.

title: Encrypted backups and a restore drill
summary: Made backups automatic with a systemd timer, encrypted them to a public key whose private half isn't on the server, and made them with a read-only user. Then restored one into a separate database, lost my own private key by mistake, and broke the job six ways, including two backups that report success and contain nothing.

title: Monitoring and alerts
summary: Added a check that runs every 5 minutes and looks at VaultLab from the outside in: health, certificate, services, backup, disk and failed units. It notifies only when the state changes. Then I broke it five ways, found that DynamicUser= breaks systemctl inside the service on this machine, and noted what a check on the same machine can't see.
